subject_session: Achilles-10252013 (figures); pooled across Achilles-10252013, Cicero-09012014, Cicero-09172014, Gatsby-08022013, Buddy-06272013

headline_stat.name: % directional place fields with significant theta phase locking (Rayleigh p<0.05)

stated_limitation: The absolute value of the preferred phase depends on recording depth, since the theta wave reverses across the CA1 layers, and one session (`Buddy-06272013`) indeed sits about 150 deg away from the other four; it is the clustering within a session, not the numerical value across sessions, that is the result.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000044 (Grosmark & Buzsáki dorsal CA1 linear-track) is the canonical known-good dataset for theta entrainment and precession, and the agent used five appropriate linear-track sessions.
justification.handling: Real data is streamed via LINDI with correct sampling-rate reconstruction, excitatory-only cell filtering, speed thresholding, directional field detection, and proper LFP conversion.
justification.analysis: Rayleigh test with a spike-jitter control and Kempter circular-linear regression with a 1000-shuffle permutation null are the standard, correct methods with the required nulls present.
justification.correctness: Every headline number reproduces from the committed CSV and is internally consistent, with only a trivial off-by-one in fitted/significant precession counts.
justification.figures: Figures clearly show phase locking, place-field tiling, and diagonal precession bands, are labeled with units and sample sizes, and choose examples by correlation/locking strength rather than slope.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence, the 57% precession fraction and depth-dependent phase offset are acknowledged, and specific real limitations are stated plainly.
justification.verdict: The work is sound, reproducible, and honestly reported end to end; I would accept it as is.
